interpretation: Among the same frozen exact-point loss/recovery sequences, points that re-record Thalassia one year after loss had a longer uninterrupted pre-loss Thalassia history than non-return points, even after stratifying within stable transect and loss-year vegetation class. This supports a local legacy/persistence signal beyond broad node quality and immediate community continuity.
ecological_boundary: The result identifies historical state dependence at the exact meter-mark scale but cannot distinguish residual rhizomes/clonal integration, fine-scale habitat quality, or observation/detection persistence.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc exploratory temporal ecology on an already-opened exact-point panel.
Do not equate the pre-loss streak signal with direct evidence of below-ground rhizome survival or clonal integration.
Return is re-recorded Thalassia at the same meter mark, not proven demographic recolonization.
